content.value_statement: Poor schemas slow teams and create data defects. This skill guides normalized models, NoSQL tradeoffs, indexing, constraints, and safe migrations.
actual_capabilities: Compares SQL normalization with NoSQL embedding and references.
Recommends indexes for foreign keys, filters, sorting, and text search.
Defines constraints for primary keys, foreign keys, uniqueness, checks, and nullability.
Outlines reversible, backward-compatible, and zero-downtime migration patterns.
Includes a schema design checklist and a reusable migration template.
limitations: Does not inspect a live database or measure real query plans.
Does not execute migrations or modify production schemas.
Examples need adaptation for each database engine and framework.
Security, compliance, and DBA review remain necessary for sensitive systems.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Product Schema
use_cases.description: Turn product requirements into tables, relationships, constraints, indexes, and migration steps before implementation.

use_cases.title: Review a Migration
use_cases.description: Check an upcoming schema change for rollback coverage, compatibility risks, and deployment sequencing.

use_cases.title: Choose SQL or NoSQL
use_cases.description: Compare relational and document models against access patterns, consistency needs, scale, and iteration speed.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Basic Schema
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a SQL schema for [product area]. List entities, relationships, primary keys, foreign keys, constraints, and initial indexes. Explain normalization choices.

prompt_templates.title: Review Existing Tables
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this schema for normalization, missing constraints, indexing gaps, and migration risks: [paste schema]. Prioritize changes by impact and effort.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Safe Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a phased migration plan from [current schema] to [target schema]. Include compatibility, backfill, validation, rollback, and deployment order.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Storage Models
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare SQL, document, and hybrid designs for [system]. Include access patterns, consistency needs, indexes, scaling limits, and migration tradeoffs.

output: Identifies customers, orders, order items, products, payments, and shipments as core entities.
Describes one-to-many and many-to-many relationships with required keys and constraints.
Recommends indexes for customer order history, payment status, and fulfillment lookup.

output_examples.input: Review a migration that renames a user email column.
output: Proposes add-copy-read-write-drop sequencing to preserve compatibility.
Calls out rollback checks, backfill validation, and monitoring points.
Warns against dropping the old column before all readers switch.

output_examples.input: Choose SQL or NoSQL for an activity feed.
output: Compares relational joins, document embedding, and hybrid fan-out storage.
Maps each option to read volume, write volume, consistency, and retention needs.
Recommends indexing and partitioning topics to validate during design.

best_practices: Start with access patterns, entities, and relationships before choosing indexes.
Use constraints for data integrity and migrations for controlled change.
Test large migrations on realistic data and keep rollback paths clear.
anti_patterns: Choosing document storage only because requirements are uncertain.
Adding indexes for every column without measuring query needs.
Making destructive schema changes before old application code is removed.

faq.question: Can this skill design both SQL and NoSQL schemas?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers relational normalization and document modeling tradeoffs.

faq.question: Does it generate migration code?
faq.answer: It provides migration structure and planning guidance. You must adapt statements to your database.

faq.question: Can it replace a database administrator?
faq.answer: No. It supports design and review, but expert review is still important.

faq.question: Does it cover performance tuning?
faq.answer: It covers indexing, query shape, N+1 avoidance, and migration performance planning.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it handle production safety?
faq.answer: It includes rollback, staging tests, compatibility, and zero-downtime migration guidance.
